clue.text: Where Orwell booked some days in the country

definitions.text: Where Orwell booked some days in the country

parts.words: Where Orwell booked some days in the country
parts.note: Orwell's first novel is about days spent in an Asian country where he served as a policeman; 'booked' means wrote a book set there

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the writer reserving a few days' holiday in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' looks like a reservation, but it means Orwell set a book there: his novel Burmese Days.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's novel Burmese Days is set in that Asian nation, where he had been a colonial policeman.

clue.text: He serves you, and gets tip in exchange

indicators.note: gets one thing in means the word for tip sits inside the word for exchange

parts.note: to barter is to exchange goods
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A waiter swaps his service for a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinks server behind a pub counter is the man who serves you.

clue.text: More actors respond thus in those like Othello

indicators.note: thus in tells the solver the answer is shown inside the words More actors

explanation.surface: Moors such as Othello respond in this way when played by more actors.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'moRE ACTors'; 'those like Othello' are Moors, punning on 'More actors' said as 'Moor actors'.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something that happens.

clue.text: Alien as " an army awfully arrayed " (Anon.)

definitions.meaning: an alien is a foreigner, here someone from Vienna's country
the anonymous alliterative verse begins 'An ___ army awfully arrayed', with the answer filling the gap

explanation.surface: A foreigner described in a line of anonymous verse about a fearsome army.
explanation.walkthrough: The well-known alliterative alphabet poem by Anon. opens 'An Austrian army awfully arrayed, Boldly by battery besieged Belgrade'.
explanation.definitionFit: To an English speaker a native of Vienna's nation is a foreigner, and the anonymous poem's army comes from there.

clue.text: Sound reply to charge of sawing woman in half?

indicators.note: sound tells the solver the answer is said like a phrase rather than spelt as it

parts.words: charge of sawing woman in half
parts.note: a magician charged with sawing a woman in half must 'rejoin 'er', put her back together

explanation.surface: A conjuror is asked to answer the charge of cutting his assistant in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejoin 'er', with the h dropped, is said like the word for a retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A rejoinder is a sharp retort or answer.

clue.text: Muscovy duck? Put it back In the oven

definitions.text: Put it back In the oven

parts.note: Muscovy is old Russia, and Russian communists are Reds
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether to return the Muscovy duck to the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscovy duck' is a breed of bird in the surface, but it splits into RED (a Russian) and O (a cricket duck, zero runs).
explanation.definitionFit: Putting food back in the oven is cooking it again, doing it over.

clue.text: Raise capital for, author

parts.note: to jack up a car is to raise it
the UK capital city

explanation.surface: Someone asks a writer to raise money for a project.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London wrote The Call of the Wild and White Fang.

clue.text: Nanook of the North (cinema version)

indicators.note: a version of the word cinema is a reworked form of its letters

explanation.surface: A note that Nanook of the North exists as a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanook of the North is a famous 1922 documentary film about an Inuit hunter, which makes 'cinema version' look like a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanook, an Arctic hunter, is a man of the ice and snow.

clue.text: Converse of the way to hell

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
a course is a way or route

explanation.surface: The opposite of the road to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converse' looks like 'opposite', but it is the verb 'talk'; the way to Dis is Dis's course.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse is to talk at length, to converse.

clue.text: The odd game of cards

definitions.meaning: a card game of melding sets and runs

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a strange card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is both a dated adjective for peculiar and a well-known card game.

clue.text: Like chords I composed with a piano

definitions.text: Like chords I composed with a piano

indicators.note: composed means these letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A musician's chords, written with a piano in mind, sound rapturous.
explanation.walkthrough: CHORDSI plus A and P are rearranged by 'composed'; the whole clue describes music like a rhapsody.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic music is free and impassioned, like a rhapsody written for the keyboard.

clue.text: Be sad about hopeless finisher backed here ?

indicators.note: backed means the whole word is written backwards
about means one word goes round another letter

parts.note: to mope is to be sad

indicators.note: the finisher of hopeless is its final letter

explanation.surface: A punter is gloomy after betting on a horse that came in last at this course.
explanation.walkthrough: MOPE around S gives MOSPE, and 'backed' turns it round; 'backed' also suits horses backed at the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is the Surrey racecourse where the Derby is run, a place where horses are backed.

clue.text: Exact, if wrong once ?

parts.note: ex means former, what was once
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether precision was once mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' looks like the adjective 'precise', but it is the verb 'demand'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact money is to demand it by force, to wring it out.

clue.text: Eat innards of a Wonderland bird ? It's chancy !

indicators.note: innards of means the word eat goes into the middle of the bird

parts.note: the Lory is a parrot in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A diner is invited to eat the insides of a bird from Wonderland, a risky dish.
explanation.walkthrough: EAT goes inside LORY (L-EAT-ORY), after A. The Lory argues with Alice in the Caucus-race chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means depending on dice or luck, hence risky.

clue.text: Demanding bid at bridge?. So Horatius made it

definitions.text: Demanding bid at bridge?. So Horatius made it

parts.words: Demanding bid at bridge?. So Horatius made it
parts.note: Horatius held the bridge so that no enemy could cross

explanation.surface: A card player's bid set beside Horatius defending the bridge over the Tiber.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatius, in Macaulay's Lays of Ancient Rome, kept the bridge into Rome so the Etruscans could not get across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A way that cannot be crossed is the state Horatius left the bridge in.

clue.text: Hymns radio distorted, for example ?

indicators.note: distorted means the letters of hymns radio are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that broadcast church music came through badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Scramble HYMNS RADIO; hymns on a crackling set are themselves an example of discord.
explanation.definitionFit: Distorted music lacks harmony, so it is an instance of discord.

clue.text: Poet's a pig, drinking water with Scotch

indicators.note: drinking means the pig takes the water inside itself

parts.note: a swine is a pig
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A poet is a pig who takes whisky with water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but says the water is a Scottish stream. BURN goes inside SWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian English poet.

clue.text: Pointedly push old or new coin around

indicators.note: around means the whole run of letters is turned the other way

parts.note: d was the old penny before decimal coinage in Britain
p is the new, decimal penny

explanation.surface: Someone nudges a coin, old or new, around a table.
explanation.walkthrough: D, OR and P read backwards. Britain's pre-1971 penny was written d; the decimal penny is p.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke with something sharp.

clue.text: Record nothing true in detective work

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
O is zero, nothing
very means true or actual, as in 'the very man'

explanation.surface: A detective finds that a record holds no truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives work by finding out hidden facts, which is making discoveries.

clue.text: Supported loser at Bannockburn, in short

indicators.note: in short means the title is cut down to its abbreviated form

parts.note: Edward the Second of England was beaten by Robert the Bruce at Bannockburn in 1314

explanation.surface: A Scottish battle's losing side was backed.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward II, written Second Ed. for short.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it formally.

clue.text: Check if rule sound

indicators.note: sound tells the solver the answer is said like the word for rule

parts.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a regulation is valid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'valid', but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to check or restrain, like a horse.

clue.text: With round shape, they can provide some storage

definitions.text: With round shape, they can provide some storage

parts.words: With round shape, they can provide some storage
parts.note: round tanks that hold a town's supply of fuel, the 'can' a large container

explanation.surface: Round containers used for storing things.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the big cylindrical tanks that held town gas, rising and falling with their contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas holders are huge circular tanks for storing fuel.

clue.text: Though in clerical garb, join up

parts.note: an alb is a white vestment worn by priests

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to tie is to join

explanation.surface: A churchman, though in vestments, enlists.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit means although, even though.

clue.text: Is in Alabama city to get things going

indicators.note: in means is goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: Something in an Alabama city is getting things moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise is to organise people or resources for action.

clue.text: Leader of his people — 20 can make him great

indicators.note: can make him great means the letters of great together with his make up the other entry

parts.note: the answer to 20 across

explanation.surface: A leader of a nation could be made great.
explanation.walkthrough: GREAT plus MOSES is an anagram of the 20 across answer, so removing GREAT from its letters leaves the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt.

clue.text: Fruit of endless combination of atoms

indicators.note: endless means the opening and closing letters of the run are lost
a combination of atoms is atom joined to atom, the word written twice

parts.note: each unit in the run is one atom

explanation.surface: A fruit made of a never-ending combination of atoms.
explanation.walkthrough: ATOMATOM, an endless string of atoms, loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato is botanically the fruit of its plant.

clue.text: Spirit one displayed in real catastrophe …

indicators.note: displayed in means one is shown inside the other letters
a catastrophe throws the word real into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ghost appears in a genuine disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catastrophe' turns REAL into AREL, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: … and intellect, which makes prosperous his master

definitions.text: and intellect, which makes prosperous his master

parts.words: and intellect, which makes prosperous his master
parts.note: following on from the spirit in the clue before, the good sense that helps a servant's employer thrive; that spirit's master is Prospero

explanation.surface: A servant's brains help his employer prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 24's spirit, Ariel, whose master in The Tempest is Prospero, giving the 'prosperous' pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is practical intelligence or common sense.

clue.text: Do as poetic waiters also do, only standing

definitions.text: Do as poetic waiters also do, only standing

parts.words: Do as poetic waiters also do, only standing
parts.note: Milton's sonnet on his blindness ends 'They also ___ who only stand and wait'

explanation.surface: Instructions to act like waiters in a poem who just stand there.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Milton's sonnet 'When I consider how my light is spent'.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve is to do a job or suffice, and Milton's patient waiters do it by standing.

clue.text: Main attack not restricted to bank

parts.note: broad means wide, not narrow or restricted
a bank is the side of a river

explanation.surface: An offensive that is not limited to the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea: a broadside is a warship firing all guns on one side at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval volley from all of one side's guns is an attack on the high seas, the main.

clue.text: Charm Samson observed in the strong

definitions.meaning: charm here is pleasantness, sugariness of manner
Samson's riddle in Judges: out of the strong came forth something pleasant, honey in a lion's carcass

explanation.surface: Samson notices attractiveness in powerful people.
explanation.walkthrough: Samson found bees' honey in the lion he had killed: 'Out of the strong came forth sweetness'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantness of manner is a kind of sugariness, and Samson's riddle names the honey's quality.

clue.text: Postpone production of French song

parts.note: de is French for of
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Someone puts off staging a French song.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay is to put off till later.
